ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
A thin string of unknown length l is fixed at point O at its upper end, and a small ball (considered as a point mass) is connected at its lower end. The height of the suspension point O from the ground is H = 5.4m. Initially, the ball is raised to point O and released from rest. After falling freely for an unknown time t, the string becomes taut. Then, within a very short (negligible) time, the string breaks. Immediately after the string breaks, the velocity of the ball is half of the velocity of the ball at the instant the string became taut. The ball then falls to the ground after a time t. Neglect air resistance and take g = 10m/s².

1. Determine the length l of the string.
2. Determine the total time it takes for the ball to fall from point O when released from rest to the ground.

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: A thin string of unknown length l is fixed at point O at its upper end, and a small ball (considered as a point mass) is connected at its lower end. The height of the suspension point O from the ground is H = 5.4 m. Initially, the ball is raised to point O and released from rest. After falling freely for an unknown time t, the string becomes taut. Then, within a very short (negligible) time, the string breaks. Immediately after the string breaks, the velocity of the ball is half of the velocity of the ball at the instant the string became taut. The ball then falls to the ground after a time t. Neglect air resistance and take g = 10 m/s². 1. Determine the length l of the string. 2. Determine the total time it takes for the ball to fall from point O when released from rest to the ground.
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: the black dot at the top of the figure is labeled O, and is the suspension point; the thin string goes vertically downward from O, with the length l marked beside it, and the lower end of the string is connected to the small ball; the vertical arrow H on the right indicates the total height from O to the ground, and the ground is drawn at the very bottom. Then reason: let the times of the two stages before and after in the problem both be t. In the first stage, the small ball freely falls from rest from O to the position where the string has just become taut, and the displacement is equal to the string length l, so l = (1/2)gt^2; at this time the speed v = gt. The string breaks within an extremely short time, and after breaking the small ball’s speed becomes 1/2 of the original, namely v0 = gt/2, with direction downward. In the second stage, the small ball continues to fall for the same time t to the ground, and the remaining height is H - l, therefore H - l = (gt/2)t + (1/2)gt^2 = gt^2. Adding this to l = (1/2)gt^2 gives H = (3/2)gt^2. Substitute H = 5.4 m, g = 10 m/s²: 5.4 = 15t^2, t^2 = 0.36, t = 0.6 s. Thus l = (1/2)×10×0.36 = 1.8 m. The total time is the previous segment t plus the later segment t, and the string-breaking time is ignored, so T = 2t = 1.2 s.
